claims.claim: OMISSION: Section 2(a)(5)(A) Termination/Revision — when a court, party, or monitor seeks to revise a monitorship, the court must conduct a hearing
claims.sourceSpan: the court shall conduct a hearing
claims.note: The hearing-on-revision requirement is one of the enumerated appointment conditions the Judicial Conference must establish, yet it is entirely absent from the analysis (summary, top_lines, sections, changes). Material: a core provision a reader would need.

claims.claim: OMISSION: Section 2(a)(5)(B) — a court may revise a requirement of a monitorship only with respect to a subject that has NOT attained substantial and sustained compliance

claims.note: This compliance-based limit on revising monitorship requirements is omitted. Especially notable because the analysis repeatedly frames the bill as having "no assessment of compliance status" — yet (a)(5)(B) introduces a "substantial and sustained compliance" standard governing revisions.

notes: Source = engrossed House text (EH), 3760 chars, no referencedSources. Material findings are two omissions: SEC. 2(a)(5) Termination/Revision (hearing requirement + "substantial and sustained compliance" standard limiting revisions) is entirely absent from the analysis, which elsewhere frames the bill as having no compliance test. Recurring minor imprecisions: "consent decree" substituted for source "court order" (broader) in summary/brief/likelihoodReason/underreported; "6 or more years" / "6+" extends source "has been in effect for 6 years"; "firm" glosses source "employer". likelihoodReason vote counts (219-204, 5 crossover) and sponsor/cosponsor facts are correct vs votes[]/metadata but not in bill text (marked UNSUPPORTED-minor per source-only stance). The McBath floor criticism/featured_quote is Congressional-Record-derived and not verifiable against the bill-text source (no CR source file registered), so no quote rows were created.
